A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DINOSaur method and continual anomaly detection benchmark. Both contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–E, supporting a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection, forgetting, edge-device efficiency, and hyperparameter-sensitivity results across five benchmark protocols.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and efficiency experiments, revises detection results, and adds pixel-level localization results and an image/pixel correlation analysis.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E retain the frozen DINOv3 backbone, spatial coresets, CLS-prototype routing, neighborhood scoring, and training/inference algorithms. The added pixel-level evaluation does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: The datasets and drift scenarios remain unchanged. However, v1 explicitly restricts evaluation to image classification, whereas v2 additionally evaluates defect localization on MVTec-AD, MVTec-LOCO, MTD-Color, and MTD-Blur in Section 5.3.

E2.justification: DNE, IUF, UCAD, PatchCore with replay, and EfficientAD with replay remain the comparison methods. Newly cited PatchcoreCL is discussed as mechanistically equivalent to the existing PatchCore baseline, without a separately evaluated entry or documented baseline modification.

E3.justification: v2 adds pixel-level AUROC evaluation, excluding geometric drift because of padding artifacts and DNE because it lacks spatial maps. Existing image-level metrics, thresholds, training budgets, resolutions, task orders, and drift parameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 adds an analysis of whether conclusions depend on image-level versus pixel-level evaluation, reporting correlation and agreement among leading methods. The existing coreset/radius sensitivity grid, forgetting analyses, and drift comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: v2 introduces image/pixel AUROC correlation reporting, with r=0.945. Edge latency still uses mean and standard deviation over 30 runs; no additional detection-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 revise DINOSaur's AUROC on all five protocols: MVTec-AD 0.963 to 0.968, LOCO 0.760 to 0.768, Color 0.888 to 0.928, Geo 0.532 to 0.519, and Blur 0.864 to 0.891. Accuracy and recall also change, including Geo recall from 1.000 to 0.050; IUF's unchanged 0.525 now exceeds DINOSaur on Geo. New Table 3 adds 20 pixel-AUROC results. These substantially revise the empirical record despite unchanged stated training settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations for drift, forgetting, feature extraction, memory, scoring, routing, and baseline losses are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation accompanies the pixel-level evaluation.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion narrow DINOSaur's performance claim from leading all five protocols to leading four, explicitly excluding geometric drift. The introduction also qualifies the edge-feasibility gap by distinguishing dedicated CAD methods from existing static or single-backbone replay work.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new correlation and localization results as evidence that its conclusions are not artifacts of metric choice, and identifies affine padding as a limitation of geometric pixel scoring. Appendix D.2 now treats IUF's numerical geometric-drift lead as practically uninformative because all methods remain near chance.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/data repository pointer in the introduction. Figure 1's caption newly explains that masks remain unchanged for color/blur and receive the same geometric transformation as images. The detailed implementation settings and pseudocode in the appendices are retained.

R1.justification: Three Barusco et al. works are added, covering medical-domain continual detection, PaSTe, and memory-efficient edge continual detection. The introduction and related work distinguish their scope, while Section 5.2 adds positioning against PatchcoreCL. The broader research framing remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 inserts a pixel-level evaluation subsection, makes targeted revisions to the abstract, introduction, related work, and discussion, and condenses the efficiency and future-work prose. The overall narrative, method exposition, and appendix organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the image/pixel comparison table, relocates and resizes existing tables, and expands Figure 1's caption. The two figure graphics and algorithm displays are retained; the document undergoes limited layout adjustments rather than a visual redesign.

improvement.justification: New Table 3 supplies empirical support for v1's largely asserted image/localization relationship, while narrower headline claims and additional related-work and access information improve clarity. These are limited gains: DINOSaur's revised scores are unexplained, and their approximately 0.815 average now conflicts with the unchanged 0.801 default-configuration average in Table 5, which matched v1. This reporting inconsistency limits confidence, but the added validation and clearer scope support a modest overall improvement.
